scope.label: one-day global observations
caveats: All figures and statistics are one-day global observations from the extracted FIRMS archives.
Raw detection counts are not a measure of sensor quality.
This date does not support a seasonal or historical conclusion.
The raw CSV files are not modified.
scope.populations: Satellite groups partition each source. Source totals are the archive row counts. Adding a source total to its satellite totals double counts the same detections.

numeric_methods.std: Sample standard deviation with divisor n-1. Null when a group has fewer than two detections.
numeric_methods.zero: Count of values exactly equal to 0. Zeros remain in the mean, the quantiles, and the extrema.
numeric_methods.extremes: Within each satellite, FRP at or above the 0.999 quantile is flagged, including ties. Flagged rows remain in every distribution. The flag is an investigation list, not a filter.

utc_time.note: acq_time is read as UTC HHMM, which is how FIRMS stores acquisition time. The hour is the first two digits. Times are not converted to local time. A single UTC hour contains many local times, so the hour histogram is not a local diurnal cycle. The daynight column is the archive flag and is not recomputed from the clock.

confidence.semantics: MODIS integer confidence stored from 0 through 100.

daynight.meaning: D and N are the stored daynight flags. They are not recomputed from local solar time.

acquisition_hour_utc.bin: UTC hour from the first two digits of acq_time

spatial_density.method: Global density uses equal-degree longitude and latitude bins. A cell near a pole covers less ground than a cell at the equator, so the maps are not equal-area. The companion rate divides each cell count by its spherical zone area on a sphere of radius 6371.0088 km and reports detections per 1,000 km². Both quantities count archived detections for this date. They do not count unique fires.

spatial_overlap.method: Spatial overlap is a proximity count between archived detections. For each ordered pair of satellites, every detection in A is assigned the nearest detection in B. The distance is the Euclidean chord length between Earth-centered coordinates on a sphere of radius 6371008.8 m. At a 5 km threshold this chord is within a millimeter of the great-circle length. A detection is counted at a threshold when that nearest distance is less than or equal to the threshold. The thresholds are configurable proximity radii, not sensor footprints. They do not account for scan-dependent pixel growth, geolocation error, or the time between acquisitions. One detection can be close to more than one other satellite. The relation is ordered, so A's share with a neighbor in B can differ from B's share with a neighbor in A. Self-pairs are omitted. Terra and Aqua are separate groups. The result is not a unique-fire match rate and no harmonization factor is calculated.

extreme_frp.rule: A row is listed when its FRP is at or above the 0.999 quantile of its own satellite, using the linear quantile method. The original CSV fields are preserved. line_number is 1-based and counts the header as line 1. No extreme row is removed from the distributions.
